scope: Unchanged-native short-prefix diagnostic, not a causal intervention or controller acceptance screen.
wrench_alignment: The five completed 1 ms solves following command row h are averaged and compared with observer interval mean at row h+1, not row h.
moment_origin: Each force sample uses the pre-solve wheel-centre position; post-solve centre is retained as sensitivity, not tuned for a best fit.
force_sets: native measurement rows: admitted and (depth>0 or signed normal force>0)
pressure: Admitted signed normal force>1e-9 N; nonpositive records remain in signed-force accounting.
rim_rule: Smooth and rim tags fold into the corresponding shell for four-family comparisons; seven raw tags are preserved separately.
inferred_family_rule: Argmax of nonzero inferred load; none if sum<=1e-9 N. Compare independently with current last-solve, prior-interval mean, and prior-interval substantial occupancy.
physical_filter: Same 100 rad/s exponential wrench filter, anchored once to saved native filtered wrench at 100.5 s. No fitted delay or filter constants.
preview_query: For each fixed focus anchor and each original target, query the first captured 1 ms sample at/after anchor+selected lookahead, tolerance1e-9 s; retain rounding lag <=1ms. No nearest-time choice optimized by outcome.
preview_semantics: Predicted patch exposure is kinematic geometry, not a forecast of force onset. Future force presence, pressure share and occupancy are descriptive associations, never an accuracy gate.
preview_motion_check: Reconstruct original constant-current-velocity geometry at selected horizon, and compare actual future pose against the SAME frozen anchor plane. Actual future pose is hindsight scoring only.
preview_surface_check: Also report future margin using future positive-pressure solver-normal aggregate. It is an aggregate contact direction, not a unique terrain plane or online input.
material_velocity: Analytic rigid-body velocity at the sampled pressure-mean point, including shaft/shell rates and previous held prescribed belt speed; projected on the sampled pressure-normal tangent. No slip/friction model is inferred from this alone.
force_projection: Downhill direction is normalized projection of gravity onto the interval pressure-normal tangent; project all signed contact force, model gravity and their sum separately. These are sampled exported-force diagnostics, not exact solver impulses, root acceleration, or motor/gravity work attribution.
COM_check: Use captured mirror-model XML masses/local inertial positions and the known zero-offset fork/carrier/shell body tree to compute whole-robot COM velocity kinematically from recorded state. Compare mass times completed-5ms COM velocity difference/dt against each signed exported-force sum plus model gravity and captured disturbance. No private physics. Keep residual/quadrature limitations and root/COM distinction explicit.
current_command_timing: Current requested/applied command acts after the recorded state. The prior actual held command generated the completed interval.

descriptive_event_rules.first_clipping: First current held request differing from box-clipped applied input within the focus window; this is not independently identified instability onset.
descriptive_event_rules.first_large_motion: First focus row with XY speed>0.1 m/s; diagnostic marker only, not a performance gate or fitted onset.
descriptive_event_rules.routing_change: Every change of argmax inferred family or argmax physical prior-interval pressure; report all, not only selected events.

required_validation: Original79field exact prefix parity before interpretation
Substep held-input identity and interval endpoint mapping
Extra-preview row identities against precision and original returned info
Reconstructed original target margins/velocities within1e-9 SI numerical tolerance
causal_limit: This unchanged replay establishes timing/algebra and prediction associations. It does not prove routing, preparation, normal lag or insufficient static motor capacity caused the departure. No new controller or physics settings.
